info.title: Gamarr API
info.description: Self-hosted game and ROM search, download, and library manager. The HTTP/JSON API powers both the SPA and any external tooling (CLI scripts, AI agents, *arr-family integrations).

apiKey.name: X-Api-Key
apiKey.description: API key for programmatic access. Also accepted via ?apikey= query parameter.

session.name: gamarr_session
session.description: Set by POST /api/login. Used by the SPA.

platform_slug.description: Platform this profile overrides; empty string = global profile. Unique across profiles when non-empty.

is_default.description: Marks the global fallback profile. Setting it clears the flag on other profiles.

region_priority.description: Ordered region preference, best first (lowered No-Intro/Redump tokens, e.g. usa, world, europe, japan).

format_preference.description: Ordered format preference, best first. Tokens: chd, cue, iso, gdi, zip, 7z, raw.

prefer_1g1r.description: Prefer verified dumps and latest revisions (one game, one ROM).

preferred_size_min.description: Size-sanity floor in bytes; 0 = built-in per-platform default.

preferred_size_max.description: Size-sanity ceiling in bytes; 0 = built-in per-platform default.

upgrade_allowed.description: Reserved for the upgrade loop; not consumed yet.

cutoff_source.description: Reserved for the upgrade loop; not consumed yet.

SearchResult.description: A single game/ROM search hit. Fields are populated per source — DDL sources omit seeders/leechers; torrent sources usually omit detail-page GUIDs.

BulkJobRequest.description: Empty or missing job_ids means 'operate on all matching jobs' (failed for retry, active for cancel).

DownloadRequest.description: POST body for /api/download. Mirrors a SearchResult row (clients may POST one verbatim) plus optional pluck and disc-set controls.

source_type.description: "ddl" routes to the direct downloader; anything else routes by download_protocol

md5.description: Expected content MD5 (archive.org); verified before a destructive convert

target_file.description: One file to pluck out of a pack torrent (#256); empty = whole content

disc_set_id.description: Disc-set membership (F4): downloads sharing an id converge into set_dir and finalize (normalize/convert/.m3u/one library row) when the last member lands. All four disc-set fields travel together.

disc_total.description: Member count the set is complete at

set_dir.description: Shared game-directory name (single path component, disc token stripped)

get.description: Per-platform selection policies (region/format priority, 1G1R flags, source ranking, size bounds).

400.description: Validation error (unknown region/format token, missing name)

409.description: Another profile already claims the platform_slug

get.description: Returns the profile plus the platforms that default to it — what deleting it would orphan.

put.description: Full-body replace: omitted fields are zeroed.

409.description: Another profile already claims the platform_slug

get.description: Liveness probe. Returns 200 if the binary is running. No auth required.
Returns this OpenAPI 3.1 document. AI agents can fetch this to discover endpoints.

Every platform in the registry — the canonical vocabulary — not only the ones already in the library, plus an "all" sentinel for filter UIs. Directories that are not platforms are excluded; library platforms with no registry row are merged in so the Library filter can reach every row it holds.

parameters.name: full
parameters.description: Return whole registry rows (identity, aliases, media class, CHD policy, acquisition switch, DAT lane) instead of the {id, name} picker shape.

get.description: The canonical row: display name, IGDB identity (slug + id), RomM fs_slug, Prowlarr and Newznab categories, media class, CHD policy, acquisition switch, and the DAT lane assigned to it.

put.description: Sparse: display_name, media_class (carts|discs|arcade|computer|pc), converts_to_chd, acquisition_enabled and default_profile_id are each left unchanged when absent. default_profile_id 0 clears the platform's default so titles fall through to the global one; a template cannot be assigned. Identity fields (slug, IGDB, RomM fs_slug, categories) are not editable — they are the vocabulary, not a preference.

get.summary: Search all configured sources for a game/ROM

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Platform slug filter, e.g. 'nes'. Omit or 'all' for cross-platform.

get.description: Returns each registered source with enabled state, circuit-breaker status, last success/fail counters.

post.summary: Retry many failed jobs at once
post.description: Empty body retries ALL failed jobs. Otherwise retries the specified job_ids.

post.summary: Cancel many active jobs at once
post.description: Empty body cancels ALL active jobs. Otherwise cancels the specified job_ids.

patch.summary: Change a wishlist entry's quality profile
patch.description: profile_id pins one title to a specific profile — "the Japanese revision of this one game", which a platform default cannot express. 0 clears the override, returning the row to whatever the platform defaults to when the cycle runs.

post.summary: Delete many wishlist items at once

get.description: Lets Prowlarr / Sonarr / other *arr apps use Gamarr as a Torznab indexer. ?t=caps returns the capabilities document; ?t=search&q=<title> returns RSS results.

200.description: Torznab XML (RSS feed or caps document)

post.summary: Start a download (DDL, torrent, or NZB)

200.description: Job created; body carries job_id and an optional duplicate-library warning

400.description: Missing URL or invalid disc-set fields

get.description: Merged runtime settings document (admin): stored DB rows where present, env-derived defaults otherwise. Keys: extract_archives, normalize_roms, convert_roms, remove_torrent_after_import, seed_janitor_enabled, scheduler_auto_download, scheduler_min_score, watcher_enabled, watcher_interval_seconds, scheduler_enabled, scheduler_interval_hours, selector_mode, selector_set_timeout_hours, romm_sync_enabled, romm_sync_interval_seconds, romm_connect_enabled, romm_exclude_platforms.

put.description: Sparse merge (admin): only keys present in the body change; values validate before anything applies. A JSON null deletes the stored row so the env default applies again; unknown keys are ignored. Loop-owning keys (watcher/scheduler/RomM sync/RomM Connect) re-arm their background loops synchronously before the response returns.

200.description: Merged settings document after the update

400.description: A declared key failed validation; nothing was applied

get.description: The built-in driver specs (vimm, archiveorg) with enabled/base_url/mapping and the computed active flag (admin).

put.description: Sparse patch {enabled?, base_url?, mapping?} (admin). The registry is a closed set: unknown names 404. Writes hot-apply — the live registry swaps before the response returns.

get.description: The built-in Vimm display row followed by custom rows with stable ids (admin).

post.description: Body {name, url} (admin). Custom rows are placeholders until a generic DDL driver consumes them.

delete.description: By stable id (admin); built-in rows have no id and cannot be deleted.

get.summary: List DAT authorities and their platform assignments (admin)
get.description: fetch_driver and fetch_base are data, not code: repointing an authority at a mirror, a CDN or a self-hosted clone is an edit rather than a deploy.

patch.description: Sparse patch of enabled, fetch_driver, fetch_base and pinned_version. A pinned version freezes automatic advance while leaving manual refresh available. fetch_base must be an absolute http(s) URL; Dat-o-Matic hosts are rejected because they ban scrapers by IP, and redump.org is rejected in favour of redump.info. Changing fetch_driver returns warnings for assignments whose dat_code no longer suits it.

200.description: Updated authority, plus warnings when a driver change invalidates assignments

post.summary: Refresh every platform assigned to an authority (admin)
post.description: Fetches sequentially with a politeness delay. A platform that fails keeps its previous snapshot, and the authority's last_status becomes ok, partial or error. Responds 200 with success=false when a refresh is already running.

400.description: Authority is disabled or has no automated fetch

post.description: multipart/form-data with a file part. This transport is required: raw bodies are capped at 1MB and a daily pack is tens of megabytes. With ?platform=<slug> the body is one catalog for that platform (bare, or a zip holding a single DAT). Without it, a zip is treated as a pack and fanned out across the authority's assignments, with unmatched members reported as skipped. Redump packs should name their platform, since a Redump dat_code is a system code rather than a DAT name.

parameters.name: platform
parameters.description: Target platform slug for a single-catalog upload

put.summary: Assign a platform to a DAT authority (admin)
put.description: dat_code is driver-specific: the libretro mirror's DAT name without extension, or a Redump system code. The pair is validated here, since a mismatched code would otherwise fail only at fetch time. There is no delete: set enabled=false to retire an assignment.

get.description: Cadence state plus the current or last run: phase, authority, progress and per-platform results.
Reads the platform's ACTIVE snapshot only. This is the catalog as the authority published it — one entry per dump, so a game the authority lists once per dump format appears once per format.

200.description: A page of catalogued dumps plus the total

get.summary: The files of one catalogued dump
get.description: A disc is several rows — the cue plus every track — which is why the files are a separate call rather than a column on the game.

200.description: The dump's files with their sizes and hashes

get.summary: The platform's 1G1R set, reconciled against the library
get.description: One keeper per game, every other catalogued dump surplus, and a readable reason on every row. Groups come from parsed titles plus the platform's clone list. Region priority ORDERS keepers and never removes one, so a game that only ever released in Japan keeps its Japanese dump. Statuses: owned (the keeper is on disk), gap (the set wants it and we do not have it), out (policy excludes the group entirely). Counts always describe the whole set, never the filtered page.

200.description: A page of set entries, whole-set counts, the policy that decided them, and the clone list in play

get.description: Phase, counts per verdict, how many files no catalog has heard of, and where the archive tree lives.

200.description: Status of the current or last declutter run

post.description: Reads the 1G1R set in the prune direction and classifies every owned dump the set does not keep, plus every library file no catalog knows. Nothing moves. A dump is only planned for archiving when the dump the set DOES keep is already on disk and the match was by hash or canonical name; a title-only match or a missing keeper is review-only. Three opt-ins widen it, each with weaker evidence than the last: include_excluded (catalogued hacks, prototypes and unlicensed dumps — archiving one removes a game rather than a duplicate), include_uncatalogued_duplicates (off-catalog files whose title is a game whose catalogued dump is already on disk), include_uncatalogued_hacks (off-catalog files whose name declares them a hack, alternate or bad dump, pirate release or fan translation). None of them can reach a file when the set is still missing that game's catalogued dump.

200.description: Preview started, or a reason it did not
A page of classified rows plus the total

post.summary: Archive the held preview's planned rows (admin)
post.description: Moves each planned file into the archive tree and appends a manifest line recording where it came from, what replaced it and why. Never deletes. exclude_ids drops rows from this apply.

200.description: Apply started, or a reason it did not

get.summary: The gap list collection mode is working through
get.description: One row per game a monitored platform's 1G1R set wants and the library does not have. A table rather than a derivation because a gap needs memory: attempts, the last result, and a backoff that doubles per attempt and caps at a week. Not the wishlist — that is what a person asked for by name; these are what a policy implies.

200.description: A page of gaps, status counts, the monitored platforms and the per-cycle pace

post.description: Reconciles every monitored platform, or one named by the platform parameter, and writes the difference. New gaps are added, existing ones keep their attempt history, and gaps that are filled or no longer wanted are removed. Synchronous — it is one reconciliation against an in-memory snapshot.

200.description: Per-platform added, removed and set counts

get.description: Which platforms carry a clone-list locator, what is stored for each, the fetch base, and whether a refresh is running. Clone lists are the upstream opinion about which differently-named dumps are the same game — the catalogs themselves ship no parent/clone data at all.

200.description: Locators, stored lists and refresh status

post.description: Asynchronous: it returns immediately and the stored rows are the status. A run already in flight returns 409.

get.description: Two independent counts. Coverage does not match owned files against catalog entries, so the numbers are presented as 'N owned, M known' and never as a completion percentage. Nothing here asserts that a file is correct.

The size band each platform's candidates are judged against. min_size and max_size are bytes, and zero on either end means that end is unbounded rather than zero bytes; a platform with both at zero is not size-filtered at all. The numbers are enforced exactly as stored, so what is listed here is what rejects. source is 'catalog' for a band derived from a DAT snapshot or 'manual' for one an operator set, and a manual row is never overwritten by a refresh. has_catalog reports whether a reset has a snapshot to re-derive from. Every platform with a catalog lane is listed even before anything has been imported for it.

put.summary: Set a platform's size bounds by hand (admin)
put.description: Stores bounds as source='manual', which a catalog refresh will not overwrite. Bounds are enforced verbatim: a value typed here is a statement about the files themselves, so nothing widens it afterwards. Zero means unbounded on that end. Omitting an end leaves it unchanged rather than clearing it. Use the reset endpoint to return to the catalog's numbers.

400.description: Invalid slug, negative bound, inverted band, or neither bound supplied

post.summary: Return a platform to its catalog-derived band (admin)
post.description: Re-derives the band from the platform's active snapshot, discarding an operator's manual bounds. With no snapshot to fall back on the definition is removed entirely, leaving the platform unbounded. There is no delete: retiring your own numbers is a reset to the authority's, which is a different thing from removing the platform.
